correspondence.component_scope: initial mountain headward run
correspondence.finding: JICA's original regional hydrological and river-system figures show the upper San Juan catchment, but their generalized and crowded linework does not securely resolve the entire selected starting branch and its westward turn. The PNJCR author's prose describes the upper San Juan running southeast to northwest and distinguishes the Río Limón basin farther south, but no plan-map pixels were obtained. This prose does not promote a regional description into exact selected-component correspondence.

correspondence.component_scope: mountain connector and sabaneta approach
correspondence.finding: The historical irrigation map places Sabaneta Dam on the San Juan corridor and shows its downstream continuity toward San Juan town. However, the selected northern approach, the reservoir/inlet interval and their branch decisions are not all legible enough for a complete component-level correspondence. INDRHI independently identifies Sabaneta as a dam on Río San Juan; its operator facts do not supply a missing map connector.

correspondence.component_scope: san juan upper valley
correspondence.finding: JICA Figures 3.2.4, 3.2.5 and 3.5.2 place the south-flowing San Juan river between the Sabaneta setting and the San Juan valley. The river can be distinguished from the separately symbolized irrigation canals and roads. This supports the generalized selected valley corridor, without deciding the unresolved northern inlet interval.

correspondence.component_scope: san juan town and southeastern valley
correspondence.finding: The original JICA maps trace San Juan past the town and southeast through the agricultural valley, with Río Mijo entering from the north and Río Los Baos from the southwest. Those incoming rivers are separate components, rather than alternate names for the selected line. The municipality's compiled city map independently depicts the San Juan channel beside the western side of San Juan de la Maguana, but contributes no mountain or terminal coverage.

correspondence.component_scope: san juan yaque junction
correspondence.finding: The regional river-system and irrigation maps establish the San Juan branch joining Yaque del Sur downstream of the separate Sabana Yegua dam setting. The selected line follows the western San Juan approach and then the common southeastward receiving trunk, rather than the Yaque's upstream mountain branch. A generalized junction interval is supported; no precise name-boundary vertex or through-Sabana-Yegua reservoir passage is asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: middle yaque and modern impoundment context
correspondence.finding: JICA Figures 3.2.5, 3.5.3 and 3.5.4 support the historical Yaque del Sur corridor downstream of Villarpando toward Los Guiros and the lower valley. Roads and irrigation transfers toward Azua remain distinct. INDRHI's current operator page identifies Montegrande on this river and gives 2024 as its operation-start year. The historical map does not depict that impoundment, and no contemporary primary map was read that resolves the selected reservoir approach, passage and outlet. The exact subset of these retained parts affected by the modern reservoir is not established.

correspondence.component_scope: tamayo vicente noble lower valley
correspondence.finding: JICA's regional and lower irrigation-district maps trace the Yaque through the lower plain between the Tamayo and Vicente Noble settings. The selected westward-to-southward course agrees at corridor scale. Irrigation headworks and canals are separately symbolized; their operating arrangements or present diversion flows are not inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: laguna rincon eastern side and actual terminal setting
correspondence.finding: JICA Figures 3.2.4, 3.2.5 and 3.5.4 show the lower river passing east of the separately depicted Laguna Rincón and reaching the Bahía de Neiba/Caribbean coastal setting north of Barahona. This supports the selected final southern and eastward approach to the coast rather than a terminal in Lago Enriquillo or Laguna Rincón. The generalized map does not establish an exact present mouth position, bank alignment or active distributary configuration.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern Miertsching Lake sheet to western Barrow River sheet — initial ponds and southeast streams
correspondence.finding: The initial selected setting is a small unnamed upland lake/pond group. Short mapped channels, including intermittent sections, link the ponds southeast across the sheet edge toward the northern Nagvaak approach. Side feeders and adjacent disconnected ponds are distinguished. No hydronym is established for this initial feeder.

correspondence.component_scope: Western Barrow River sheet and adjoining eastern Miertsching Lake sheet — nagvaak northern arm and lake passage
correspondence.finding: The selected corridor enters the long northern arm of Nagvaak Lake, turns south through its connected arms, and follows its western lake passage across the sheet edge. Other arms and a rapids-marked feeder from the east are visible. The lake label identifies the lake, not a representative name for the entire selected line.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern margin of Miertsching Lake sheet — southwest lake transfers
correspondence.finding: The selected passage continues from the western Nagvaak arm through the short southward lake/channel chain associated with Tasiruluk Lake, then turns southwest through the elongated waterbody immediately south of it toward Qukuttalik Lake. The narrow links and neighboring parallel lake arms are readable. Lake names are not converted into river names.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastern Miertsching Lake sheet — qukuttalik lake and southern outlet
correspondence.finding: The selected corridor traverses Qukuttalik Lake toward its southwestern arm, leaves through a rapids-marked narrow reach and continues through the smaller southern lake chain. A substantial northern lake/river inlet, other western tributary lakes and eastern side waters are separately depicted.

correspondence.component_scope: South-central Miertsching Lake sheet — lower inland loop and ujarasugjulik approach
correspondence.finding: The source depicts the southwestward sequence of short streams and irregular lakes, its westward then northward bend and its turn south into the lake chain approaching Ujarasugjulik Lake. The relevant stream reaches, lake narrows and side feeders are visible at ordinary corridor scale. This observation does not close the following junction into Kannak/Niuninga.

correspondence.component_scope: Ujarasugjulik Lake, Kannak Lake and the labelled Tasirjuaq/Tasirjuak river junction — ujarasugjulik kannak selected transfer
correspondence.finding: The original maps the Ujarasugjulik approach near the separately labelled river connecting the Miertsching/Kannak lake area with Tuurvik Lake toward Lyon Inlet. The printed fish-resource note explicitly associates Kannak, Miertsching and Ujarasugjulik lakes with Tasirjuak River. The selected model turns southwest toward Kannak/Niuninga instead of following the eastward river corridor. At this junction, thematic overprinting and the generalized channel drawing do not unambiguously establish the selected transfer from the Ujarasugjulik approach into Kannak/Niuninga, or distinguish it from the adjacent river branch. The model line and the prose association cannot supply that missing correspondence. This is not a claim that an actual connection is absent.
correspondence.name_scope: Separately mapped river component; not adopted as a representative name for the selected chain.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern Miertsching Lake sheet and northern Hurd Channel sheet — niuninga to tasers lake
correspondence.finding: Niuninga Lake and its southern arm are mapped separately from the named eastward river corridor. The selected southern continuation corresponds to the lake passage and short connection into Tasers Lake across the sheet edge. This downstream local correspondence is independent of the unresolved entrance through the Kannak junction.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern Hurd Channel sheet, western Ross Bay — tasers outlet and western ross bay terminal
correspondence.finding: The selected lower reach corresponds to the southern Tasers Lake outlet channel, its southward approach past the slope/hachure-marked reach and its junction with a western side stream before entering western Ross Bay. The receiving bay connects to Lyon Inlet. This actual terminal is geographically distinct from the more northeasterly Tuurvik Lake/Tasirjuaq river setting. No river hydronym is printed on this final selected outlet in the inspected source; no surveyed mouth point or present tidal boundary is asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Headward dashed feeder in the Hacienda Huanana–Laguna–Santa Rosa setting into the named Chinama course near Burras/Carrizal
correspondence.finding: The original MTC sheet shows a dashed northern headward drainage passing the Hacienda Huanana/Laguna and Santa Rosa setting and joining the river at the Burras–Carrizal reach. The selected opening follows this generalized setting. The isolated settlement named Laguna is not treated as evidence of a lake passage. The feeder has no independently read local hydronym.

correspondence.component_scope: Río Chinama west through Cruz Verde, El Higuerón, Cordal and Marripón/La Arena to the Chóchope junction near Motupe
correspondence.finding: MTC maps the named westward river and its southwesterly approach through Marripón, La Arena and El Arrozal. Near Motupe the selected receiving corridor joins the eastern Río Chóchope course before continuing past Puente Motupe. PEOT independently separates this selected eastern approach from the Chotoque bypass farther west. The name Chinama is confined to its mapped reach; no formal transition point is asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Motupe south through the Motupe and Chicoma bridge settings, Anchovira/Puerto Rico and Pampa de Lino
correspondence.finding: MTC and PEOT trace the selected southward receiving course from Motupe through the bridge and valley sequence, past the eastern tributary junction in the Anchovira/Salas setting, to the bend north of Jayanca. PEOT prints Motupe on this trunk and distinguishes the western Chotoque channel. No adjacent reservoir or separate Olmos channel is transferred onto the selected route.

correspondence.component_scope: Pampa de Lino bifurcation, western Motupe arm through San Juan/Santa Lucía, and continuation toward the Panamericana crossing
correspondence.finding: INGEMMET figures 2, 9 and 10 identify the bifurcation and western arm, distinct from the eastern branch past Jayanca and Pacora toward Las Juntas. The selected line follows the western setting. INGEMMET prose says this arm meets a canal diverted from La Leche and reaches the La Niña sector. The far-west continuation and its precise material canal/river connection are not traced throughout the selected corridor in the inspected originals; the MTC sheet omits much of this linework.
correspondence.material_gap: Original-map correspondence remains incomplete between the mapped western arm and the selected downstream road-crossing/depression connector. Prose establishes a destination relationship but does not close that mapping gap.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected lower southwest and northward bend beyond the Motupe/Mórrope road crossing toward the southern La Niña depression
correspondence.finding: MTC places the selected line in the lower Mórrope desert near the mapped Panamericana bridge sequence and southern lagoon/depression margin. It does not depict a continuous hydrographic connector following the selected southwest bend and subsequent northward course. The candidate Motupe name is not extended across these unverified segments.
correspondence.material_gap: Continuous selected desert-to-lagoon connector and its relation to the mapped waterbody margins remain unresolved.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwestern transit through the Laguna La Niña depression toward the coast
correspondence.finding: The Lambayeque and Sechura sheets depict broad lagoon/depression waterbodies and the La Niña label in this lower setting. These originals give geographic context for much of the selected northwestern course, but do not establish its entire passage and connectors as one flowing channel. The flood report supports Motupe water reaching La Niña, not the selected internal lake route.
correspondence.material_gap: A basin label or broad waterbody polygon does not establish all selected lake/depression connectors.

correspondence.component_scope: Final selected southwest turn from the La Niña margin to the Pacific shore
correspondence.finding: Both adjoining MTC originals show the lagoon/coastal setting. No readable river or outlet line establishes the selected final crossing of the coast. The retained model terminal class sea is not independent hydrographic evidence. This observation does not claim that a transient overflow could never occur.
correspondence.material_gap: The actual terminal connection to the Pacific is unestablished; this is a material source-correspondence gap, not merely unresolved naming scope.

correspondence.component_scope: Extreme eastern headward opening and northward approach
correspondence.finding: The selected initial short reach lies west of the international divide and follows a small headward drainage westward, then turns north through the mapped wet valley toward upper Cisnes. IGN independently depicts this opening and turn. MMA starts slightly farther downstream, then follows the same northward valley and places Río Cisnes labels on the connected upper course. Nearby Los Materos and Los Perdidos are separate entering streams; the selection does not follow Arroyo Los Patos as its first branch. The starting point is not declared the official river source, and its small-feeder name remains unassigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Cisnes westward turn to Cáceres junction
correspondence.finding: After the northward approach, the selected trunk turns west past the Arroyo Los Patos and La Turbina surroundings, then southwest along the repeatedly mapped Cisnes course. It receives separate Las Lagunas, Angostura, Winchester and Pedregoso drainage approaches before the Cáceres junction. The continuous mapped corridor, junction sequence and distinctive bend establish geographic correspondence rather than reliance on a nearby name. No selected major lake passage is shown on this upper mainstem.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected Cáceres branch and Cisnes junction
correspondence.finding: The selected northern branch begins on the mapped Cáceres corridor, bends southeast and then south to meet the Cisnes near the transition between the two mainstem fragments. MMA explicitly distinguishes Río Cáceres from the receiving Cisnes and depicts its continuation beyond the selected beginning. Upstream Estero Carlota and other unselected tributaries are not made part of the selected branch. No lake interior is selected on this fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Cáceres junction to middle Cisnes
correspondence.finding: Below the Cáceres confluence, the selected trunk continues west along the mapped Cisnes corridor, with separate south-side Moro and later Carante o Grande approaches and north-side small drainage junctions. The original overview depicts the entire inter-fragment connection. The model fragment boundary is not used as a hydronym-change point.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle and lower Cisnes
correspondence.finding: The long western fragment follows the mapped Cisnes through its alternating bends and constricted valley settings. The source separately depicts the Torcaza, Las Torres/Travieso, Grande, Sandoval and western smaller tributary approaches. The selected line remains on the receiving Cisnes, rather than turning south toward the Las Torres lake drainage or the separate Picacho branch. Original wetland mapping corroborates its connected river/floodplain corridor; no broad mainstem lake traversal is inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern Picacho approach and first elongated waterbody passage
correspondence.finding: The southern selected branch begins within the lower Picacho drainage corridor, downstream from a readable Río Picacho label, and proceeds west to northwest through a widening water-and-wetland valley. The mapped stream approaches and the COT Cuerpos de agua polygons together show the selected passage into and along an elongated waterbody, followed by a narrower northward connection. Estero El Quique and other surrounding tributaries are distinct. A single river name is not assigned to the full waterbody passage; the report places this area within the Picacho/Presidente Roosevelt and Escondida receiving drainage, but it does not establish an exact name boundary for this selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern lake passage to lower Cisnes
correspondence.finding: From the previous southern fragment, the selected route turns north through a narrow water corridor and then a broader north–south elongated lake surface. COT explicitly classifies the selected broad surface as Cuerpos de agua, while the wetland inventory corroborates the linked continental-water corridor. The selection exits its northern end toward the lower Cisnes mouth-channel network. This is the Escondida-drainage connection described by the report, not an extension of the Cisnes name over each lake interior. The separately mapped Río Sur o María enters from the southwest and is not the selected southern source branch. Exact lake/river name-change points and current inlet/outlet positions remain unassigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Cisnes convergence and actual selected coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: The western trunk reaches the Cisnes meander-and-floodplain network, where the selected southern lake drainage joins near the coastal outlet. MMA maps the receiving river and its distinct lower loops; COT and wetland originals locate the connected lower water corridor and landward coastal opening. The short terminal fragment extends from this confluence/outlet setting into the immediate coastal water at Puerto Cisnes bay on the eastern side of Canal Puyuhuapi. It is not extended through the whole canal or to the open Pacific. Generalized model shortcuts across lower bends are not treated as exact current channels, and the sea metadata is supported at coastal-setting scale rather than at an exact mouth vertex.
